TOW Missile Launcher.name: TOW Missile Launcher
TOW Missile Launcher.description:
@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02heavyweaponh00]{Heavy Weapon}. A wire-guided missile fired from a portable or vehicle-mounted launcher. Doesn’t require a lock—just a @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll, and can’t be jammed. @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.JournalEntry.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{Medium Blast Template}.

Unless otherwise noted, missiles must “lock” onto their targets before they can be fired. This action is an opposed @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Electronics]{Electronics} roll versus the target’s maneuvering skill (@Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Boating]{Boating}, @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Driving]{Driving}, or @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Piloting]{Piloting}, as appropriate). Success gives the attacker a “short” lock and allows him to fire up to half the missiles his particular craft can fire at once. A raise is a more solid lock and allows him to fire all of them.

The enemy attempts to evade each missile separately by making a maneuvering roll at −4 (or −2 if the target has substantial cover to hide behind—such as asteroids, skyscrapers, canyon walls, or even large enemy ships. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} means the craft goes @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-tables.Out of Control]{Out of Control}.

Anti-Missile Systems: Warships and futuristic space vessels often have “point defense” systems to shoot down incoming missiles. Operators must be on @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03hold0000000000]{Hold} to shoot down missiles; automated systems attack automatically. The system grants a single @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll per missile at Short @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02range000000000]{Range} and any other relevant modifiers (including @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03speed000000000]{Speed}—missiles move at Mach 1, a −6 penalty, unless otherwise noted). Unless otherwise noted, missiles are objects with a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.JournalEntry.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03breakingthin00]{Toughness} of 8 (2).

16 to 46 Cannons (12 lb), Solid Shot (Fi.name: 16 to 46 Cannons (12 lb), Solid Shot (Fixed Left and Right)
16 to 46 Cannons (12 lb), Solid Shot (Fi.description:
Cannons are used to destroy city walls or break up large troop formations. The leader of the weapon’s crew makes the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll.

Bombard: Assuming they have a rough idea of their target’s location, howitzers, mortars, and bombards may fire at targets they cannot see by lobbing projectiles over intervening terrain or obstacles. Bombarding suffers a −4 penalty in addition to all other modifiers, and doubles deviation when the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll is failed (see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{Area Effect Attacks}). Reduce the penalty to −2 with precise coordinates (such as from a spotter).

Solid Shot: Heavy balls of iron, lead, or stone designed to batter walls or plow through packed ranks of troops. To fire, the leader of the crew makes a @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll as usual. If successful, roll a die. If even, it bounces to another victim behind and within 6” of the first and hits him as well. Continue in this way until the die roll is odd.

Compare the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll to every target within using a base TN of 4, adjusted for each target’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03coverandobst00]{cover}, special abilities like the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Dodge]{Dodge} Edge, etc. A hit causes 2d6 damage and a raise causes 3d6.

Note: All types of shot are @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.JournalEntry.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02heavyweaponh00]{Heavy Weapon (HW)}, @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02reload00000000]{Reload} 8. Two crew members may reload at the same time.

Catapult (Fixed Front).name: Catapult (Fixed Front)
Catapult (Fixed Front).description:
@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{Medium Blast Template}

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02heavyweaponh00]{Heavy Weapon (HW)}, Reload time is every 5 minutes with a crew of 4.

Catapults are simple devices that hurl large stones at enemy defenses or ranks of troops. They normally require a crew of eight to load the projectile, crank down the lever that propels it, then sight and aim it. Firing can be done by a single person, but @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03reloading00000]{loading} the projectile takes at least four.

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02heavyweaponh00]{Heavy Weapon}

Machine guns are heavy, fully automatic weapons built to withstand prolonged fire. Most are fed by belts or drums and thus have far more ammo capacity than assault rifles, despite similar calibers and rates of fire.

Weapon Mount: Most machine-guns require a @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-equipment.Bipod/Tripod]{Bipod/Tripod} or vehicle mount to fire, which eliminates any Strength requirement and the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03recoil00000000]{Recoil} penalty. Their @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02minimumstren00]{Minimum Strength} is listed as “NA,” or “Not Applicable.” If a weapon has a Minimum Strength listed, it may be fired from the hip with the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02snapfire000000]{Snapfire} and Recoil penalties.

Minimum Rate of Fire: Machine-guns have a minimum @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02rateoffire0000]{Rate of Fire} of 2 unless otherwise noted.

Reloading: Machine guns are @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02reload00000000]{Reload} 2, which includes changing belts or drums, cocking, etc.

Sidewinder Missiles.name: Sidewinder Missiles
Sidewinder Missiles.description:
@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02heavyweaponh00]{Heavy Weapon (HW)}. A short range, heat-seeking missile fired from an aircraft.

Unless otherwise noted, missiles must “lock” onto their targets before they can be fired. This action is an opposed @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Electronics]{Electronics} roll versus the target’s maneuvering skill (@Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Boating]{Boating}, @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Driving]{Driving}, or @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Piloting]{Piloting}, as appropriate). Success gives the attacker a “short” lock and allows him to fire up to half the missiles his particular craft can fire at once. A raise is a more solid lock and allows him to fire all of them.

The enemy attempts to evade each missile separately by making a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.JournalEntry.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04chasesandveh00]{maneuvering} roll at −4 (or −2 if the target has substantial cover to hide behind—such as asteroids, skyscrapers, canyon walls, or even large enemy ships. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} means the craft goes @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-tables.Out of Control]{Out of Control}.

Anti-Missile Systems: Warships and futuristic space vessels often have “point defense” systems to shoot down incoming missiles. Operators must be on @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03hold0000000000]{Hold} to shoot down missiles; automated systems attack automatically. The system grants a single @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll per missile at @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02range000000000]{Short Range} and any other relevant modifiers (including @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03speed000000000]{Speed}—missiles move at Mach 1, a −6 penalty, unless otherwise noted). Unless otherwise noted, missiles are objects with a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01characters0000]{Toughness} of 8 (2) (see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03breakingthin00]{Breaking Things}).
